mstts:express-as.prosody:
As we wrap up, let's bring everything together. Here are some key things to keep in mind: Start by noticing those ego states—the parent, the adult, and the child—in both yourself and the people you interact with. Pay attention to the familiar games and scripts that keep popping up in your relationships and in how you see yourself. When you can, try reaching for those authentic, adult-to-adult conversations. That’s where honest and meaningful communication really happens. If you spot an old pattern or game, just call it out—give it a name—and choose a new way to respond. And remember, these ideas aren’t just for work or family, but for every place you connect with others. Even small changes can really shift the energy in your relationships.
The journey to building more authentic connections isn’t about getting it perfect. It’s about showing up with intention, and being present. Each time you pause and notice a pattern, you open a door to change. Every honest conversation—awkward as it might feel—is a step closer to real connection. And if you notice some old games coming back when you’re stressed or in familiar settings, that’s totally normal. The goal isn’t to wipe out all your patterns overnight, but to notice them, and choose differently when you can. Over time, this awareness leads to more freedom, more resilience, and genuine joy in your relationships. So trust that even small steps matter. Every moment you choose to connect more honestly is a gift—to yourself, and to everyone around you. Here’s to more genuine conversations, healthier connections, and the courage to step into new ways of relating—one moment at a time.
